title: CBP officers discover individual hidden inside gas tank at San Ysidro crossing
text:
U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officers discovered a person hidden inside a vehicle’s gas tank at the San Ysidro Port of Entry, rescuing them from a life-threatening situation and arresting the driver in an attempted smuggling case.
Emergency personnel took the person to Scripps Mercy Hospital in Chula Vista for treatment of burn injuries sustained during the smuggling attempt.
Incident Details Date & Time: February 27, 2026, at approximately 7:30 p.m. Location: San Ysidro Port of Entry, the busiest land border crossing between the U.S. and Mexico. Vehicle: A 2005 GMC SUV driven by a 20-year-old man. Discovery: A CBP canine team alerted officers to the vehicle’s undercarriage. Upon secondary inspection, officers found a Mexican national concealed in a non-factory compartment built into the gas tank area . Health & Safety The individual suffered burn injuries during the smuggling attempt. Emergency personnel transported them to Scripps Mercy Hospital in Chula Vista for treatment. CBP officials emphasized the dangerous and inhumane tactics used by smugglers, who often prioritize profit over human lives. Official Statement San Ysidro Port Director Mariza Marin praised the vigilance of CBP officers, noting that their professionalism prevented a potential tragedy. She reaffirmed CBP’s commitment to disrupting smuggling operations that endanger both migrants and the public.
Legal Action The driver was arrested and booked into the Metropolitan Correctional Center in San Diego . Authorities are investigating the case further, with charges expected to follow. The incident highlights the extreme risks migrants face when subjected to smuggling operations. CBP officials warn that concealment in hazardous compartments like gas tanks can lead to severe injury or death, underscoring the need for continued vigilance at border crossings.
Source: NBC News
Baja California Post
